item.title: Capital Budget 2027-2028 prioritizes needs to build a strong foundation for tomorrow
item.description:
Capital Budget 2027-2028 prioritizes needs to build a strong foundation for tomorrow jenniferdhogan Tue, 11/10/2026 - 15:35

Today, Minister of Finance and Affordability Jill Burridge presented the Government of Prince Edward Island’s 2027-28 Capital Budget, a five-year $1.34 billion capital plan, to the Legislative Assembly.

“Prince Edward Island today is not the same PEI it was ten or twenty years ago, and Islanders’ expectations of government have evolved too. To deliver the services Islanders expect, we have to close the infrastructure gaps that remain. Today’s budget does that by focusing our capital investments where the needs are most pressing.”

- Premier of Prince Edward Island Rob Lantz

The 2027-28 Capital Budget reduces five-year planned spending by $289 million from last year’s plan. Major projects are nearing completion, construction is paced to reflect the realities of a competitive construction market, and government is balancing investments within its fiscal guardrails while protecting essential healthcare and education services.

“Our five-year capital plan is focused on getting the basics right by building the strong foundation Prince Edward Island needs to go into the future. We need healthcare and education systems that work for Islanders. That’s why nearly 60% of our five-year plan is dedicated to these essential services; we are taking care of what we already have, renewing aging infrastructure, and building new where it is needed,” said Minister of Finance and Affordability Jill Burridge. “We are going to do this responsibly, spending what we can at a pace we can afford, because this is what Islanders depend on us to do.”

Close to 60% of the Capital Budget plan presented today is dedicated to maintaining healthcare services and public education for Islanders by focusing investments in maintaining and repairing existing assets and infrastructure, and strategically investing in new projects to align with population growth and service demands. 

Five-year highlights of the Capital Budget include: 

A safe and reliable healthcare system - $418 million

  • Three Rivers Health Campus that delivers modern care for Eastern PEI - $113 million
  • Mental health campus completion - $69 million 
  • QEH critical systems for boilers, chillers, and generators - $40 million
  • Modernizing access to healthcare information - $20 million
  • With the support of PCH and QEH foundations ($33 million), replacing and renewing critical healthcare equipment and repairing facilities - $98 million 
  • Expanding public long-term care - $16 million
  • Increasing access to primary care - $19 million

Taking care of our schools and building where needed - $380 million

  • New Summerside school - $80 million
  • Completing and renewing high schools - $23 million
  • Expanding and new intermediate schools - $58 million
  • Renovating and new elementary schools - $62 million
  • Strengthening French language education - $69 million
  • School Revitalization Fund and capital repairs - $33 million
  • Safe Rides to School - $23 million
  • Classroom Technology - $20 million

Connecting communities and strengthening the economy - $370 million

  • Rehabilitating and improving roads, bridges, and highways - $285 million
  • Protecting our land and shorelines - $15 million
  • Heavy equipment and fleet renewal - $27 million
  • Boosting economic infrastructure - $15 million

Continuing housing progress - $60 million

  • Taking care of existing public housing - $25 million
  • More social housing and infrastructure - $26 million
  • Residential group homes for youth - $5 million

For more information on the 2027-28 Capital Budget, visit PrinceEdwardIsland.ca/Capital-Budget.

item.title: Statement by Minister Deagle on Nurse Practitioner Week
item.description:
Statement by Minister Deagle on Nurse Practitioner Week jenniferdhogan Tue, 11/10/2026 - 15:26

Minister of Health and Wellness Cory Deagle issued the following statement to recognize Nurse Practitioner Week:

“Nurse Practitioner Week, November 8-14,  is an opportunity to recognize and thank the dedicated nurse practitioners who provide exceptional care to Islanders every day.

Nurse practitioners are a vital part of Prince Edward Island's health care system. They work across primary care, hospitals, long-term care, mental health and addictions services, and specialized care settings, helping Islanders access timely, high-quality care closer to home.

Their expertise, compassion, and commitment make a meaningful difference in the lives of patients and families across our province. Whether they are managing complex health conditions, supporting prevention and wellness, or providing ongoing primary care, nurse practitioners play an essential role in delivering patient-centred care.

Prince Edward Island is fortunate to have one of the strongest nurse practitioner workforces in the country. Our government remains committed to supporting nurse practitioners to work to their full scope of practice and to continuing to grow this important workforce. This year alone, Health PEI welcomed 20 new nurse practitioners, helping strengthen access to care for Islanders.

I would also like to recognize the leadership of the Prince Edward Island Nurse Practitioner Association and thank its members for their advocacy and ongoing commitment to advancing the profession.

To all nurse practitioners across Prince Edward Island, thank you for your professionalism, your dedication, and the care you provide every day. Your work improves the health and well-being of Islanders and strengthens our health care system.”

item.title: Statement by Premier Lantz on Remembrance Day
item.description:
Statement by Premier Lantz on Remembrance Day jenniferdhogan Tue, 11/10/2026 - 14:46

Premier Rob Lantz issued the following statement on Remembrance Day:  

“Tomorrow, we remember Canadians who gave their lives in service to our country. We honour our veterans and those who continue to serve, and recognize the families who have shared in their sacrifices.

In communities across Prince Edward Island, Islanders will gather to lay wreaths and stand together in silence. For some, remembrance is deeply personal. It is a photograph, a story passed down, or the absence of someone they loved. For others, it is an opportunity to better understand the service and sacrifice that have shaped our country.

Each name on our cenotaphs belongs to someone who had a life here at home, people who loved them and plans for their future. To remember is to think about who they were, as well as what they gave.

The effects of service do not always end when someone comes home. Many veterans carry injuries, both visible and invisible. They and their families deserve our gratitude, our care and our support throughout the year.

Tomorrow morning at 11 a.m., I encourage all Islanders to observe a moment of silence. Whether you are attending a ceremony or pausing wherever you may be, please join in remembering those who did not return and honouring all who have served.

Lest we forget.”

item.title: New members appointed to Environmental Advisory Council
item.description:
New members appointed to Environmental Advisory Council jenniferdhogan Tue, 11/10/2026 - 14:37

The Environmental Advisory Council has been re-established to provide independent advice to government on environmental issues in Prince Edward Island.

The council brings together members representing a range of sectors and perspectives, including agriculture, fisheries, tourism, industry, municipalities, environmental organizations and conservation interests. During the first year, the council will advise government on water allocation and emerging pressures on the province’s water resources. 

“Water is one of Prince Edward Island’s most important resources, and decisions about how we manage it today will have impacts for future generations to come. We have brought together people with a wide range of knowledge, experience, and perspectives to help us work through some complex questions we are facing. I want to thank each member for stepping forward and committing their time and expertise to this important work.” 

- Minister of Land and Environment Darlene Compton

Current council members include: 

  • John MacQuarrie, chair
  • Ron Maynard, vice-chair
  • Rebecca Ramos Armstrong
  • Carolyn Peach Brown
  • Les Burridge
  • Cassandra Gautreau
  • Matthew Jelley
  • Debbie Johnston
  • Krista Shaw
  • Peter Warris

Advice from the council on water-related issues will include considerations for managing water resources in areas at or nearing capacity, applications from new users in areas with limited available capacity, surface water withdrawals, and the management of irrigation and water storage ponds.

This work will complement the Department of Land and Environment’s existing responsibilities under the Water Act, including legislation, policies, permitting, monitoring, and technical water management. The council will provide recommendations to help guide transparent, sustainable, and evidence-based decisions about water resources in the province. 

The Environmental Advisory Council is established under the Environmental Protection Act and serves as an advisory body to the Minister of Land and Environment. Over the years, the council has provided advice on important environmental issues, including the development of the Water Act.

Members of the council are appointed from those who apply through Engage PEI. 

For more information, visit Environmental Advisory Council. 

 

Media contact:
Morgan Martin
Department of Land and Environment
902-218-3430
mxmartin@gov.pe.ca

 

Backgrounder:

John MacQuarrie of Charlottetown, Queens County, is retired and held various senior leadership roles in the province in agriculture and environment.  John represents the interests of the environment sector and will serve as Chairperson for the Council. 

Ron Maynard of Tyne Valley, Prince County, has served the Council since 2015 representing the PEI Federation of Agriculture. A McGill University graduate, Ron has been actively involved in the dairy industry at the provincial and national levels for over 40 years. He will continue to represent the agriculture sector and serve as Vice-Chair of the Council.

Rebecca Ramos Armstrong of Charlottetown, Queens County is a monitoring specialist for the salmon, river otter, and bat monitoring program.  Rebecca Ramos Armstrong represents the interests of the environment and conservation sectors.

Carolyn Peach Brown of Charlottetown, Queens County, is a retired academic of environmental studies. Carolyn Peach Brown represents the interests of the environment and conservation sectors.

Les Burridge of Stratford, Queens County, has worked as an environmental scientist for over 40 years, with a focus on aquaculture. Les Burridge represents the interests of the fisheries sector.

Cassandra Gautreau of Dunstaffnage, Queens County, is the current representative nominated by the Federation of PEI Municipalities, where she currently serves as a Programs Officer. Cassandra has a background in environmental science and land use planning and practical experience in community-focused sustainability efforts. 

Matthew Jelley of Granville, Queens County, is a non-practicing member of the PEI Law Society and has been a successful entrepreneur in the tourism industry for multiple decades. Matthew Jelley represents the interests of the tourism sector. 

Debbie Johnston of Three Rivers, Kings County has previously served on the Council as a nominee for the Federation of PEI Municipalities while she was the Mayor of Three Rivers. Prior to that, Debbie had a 28-year career in air quality and hazardous materials and is continuing as a member of the Council representing the interests of the environment sector.

Krista Shaw of Stanhope, Queens County, is the Director of Stakeholder Relations at the PEI Potato Board and has experience in federal, provincial and municipal governments. Krista will represent the interests of the agriculture sector.

Peter Warris of Charlottetown, Queens County, is the current Executive Director of the PEI Aquaculture Alliance, having been involved with the association for two decades. Peter Warris represents the interests of the industry sector.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
